newsitem.title: USA: Reputed mob chief, eight others indicted in Fla..
newsitem.headline: Reputed mob chief, eight others indicted in Fla..

text.p: Nicholas "Little Nick" Corozzo, the alleged leader of New York's powerful Gambino crime family, was indicted on charges of running a mob operation in south Florida, U.S. prosecutors said Wednesday.

Corozzo, 56, reportedly named head of the Gambino family when reputed mob chieftain John Gotti was jailed for life, was arrested along with associate Ralph Davino, 53, as he sunbathed at an exclusive hotel in Key Biscayne where he was vacationing.
The posh island enclave, connected to Miami by a bridge and causeway, once was the home of Richard Nixon's winter White House.
"I don't think they were expecting this," Miami U.S. Attorney William Keefer said.

Indicted along with Corozzo and Davino were seven Gambino family "members and associates" on charges that they ran a criminal enterprise called the South Florida Crew, a branch of the Gambino family involved in loansharking and stolen property, prosecutors said.
The New York Daily News reported last year that Gotti, the mob chieftain now jailed for life, had agreed to turn over the reins of the Gambino family to Corozzo, a Brooklyn-based underling.
Gotti made the agreement under pressure from rival crime families in order to avert a bloody and protracted leadership struggle, the report said.
Keefer called Corozzo "an alleged captain and currently the ruling member of the Gambino crime family."

The 20-count indictment alleged the group was running a loansharking operation from a business called E-Z Check Cashing Inc. in Deerfield Beach, Florida. Prosecutors said they will seek forfeiture of the business and $150,000 cash.

It also accused some of the defendants of trying to torch a Boynton Beach, Florida, print shop and conspiring to murder an associate and now-federal witness, Louis Maione, suspected by the Gambino family of skimming money from its south Florida operations.

In addition to Corozzo and Davino, the indictment named Leonard DiMaria, 55, of Brooklyn; Anthony Ruggiano, 43, of Lindenwood, New York; David Furman, 30, of Deerfield Beach, Florida; Sydney Alwais, 60, and David Alwais, 30, both of Boca Raton, Florida; Salvatore Pecchio, 42, of Sunrise, Florida; and Robert Engel, 42 of Woodhaven, New York.
Corozzo, DiMaria, Davino, Ruggiano and Furman were in custody Wednesday, authorities said. The others were being sought.
The defendants faced sentences of 20 years in prison and fines of up to $250,000 on each count, prosecutors said.
